Snap Pea Salad with Sweet Chili Dressing

Published: 10/06/2026
Author: Jenn Laughlin
Comment
Jump to Recipe Pin the Recipe
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:58
Instaread

This healthy Snap Pea Salad is tossed in a delicious sweet chili dressing and packs a perfect blend of fiber, protein, and flavor!

Fibermaxxing may be all the rage right now, but getting a boatload of fiber has always been a key part of my salad recipes. Around here we’ve been scarfing dense bean salads way before they were trendy.

Honestly I hope this is more than just a viral trend because if it helps more people fall in love with eating beans and vegetables, then we are def taking a step in the right direction!

Today’s tasty salad combines sugar snap peas, edamame, scallions, and sesame seeds with a super flavorful sweet chili dressing.

This rockin’ recipe boasts 17 grams of protein 10 grams fiber per serving.

The sweet chili dressing is a perfect pairing for this lettuce free salad. I have it on pretty good authority that it’s also amazing on a fresh cucumber salad with chopped avocado thinly sliced red onion. Delish!

However you serve it, it’s sure to be a hit!

Snap pEA sALAD WITH sWEET cHILI dRESSING

This salad can be enjoyed all on it’s own as a light lunch or paired with your favorite protein for a delish (and easy!) weeknight dinner. It’s positively amazing paired with Honey Garlic Tofu as a vegetarian option or Spicy Sriracha Shrimp if you’d like a pescatarian option.

I feel like it would also be stellar alongside my Spicy Sesame Ramen Noodles — I am so trying that combo next time around!

Snap Pea Salad with Sweet Chili Dressing

This healthy Snap Pea Salad is tossed in a delicious sweet chili dressing and packs a perfect blend of fiber, protein, and flavor!
No ratings yet
Print Recipe Pin Recipe Rate Recipe
Course: Salad
Cuisine: Vegetarian
Keyword: Snap Pea Salad, Sweet Chili Dressing
Prep Time: 15 minutes minutes
Total Time: 15 minutes minutes
Servings: 2 servings
Author: Jenn Laughlin – Peas and Crayons

Ingredients

  • 8 oz snap peas
  • 8 oz shelled edamame
  • 3 TBSP sliced green onions or scallions
  • 1 TBSP toasted sesame seeds for topping, optional

SWEET CHILI DRESSING

  • 2-3 TBSP rice vinegar to taste
  • 2 TBSP sweet chili sauce
  • 2 TBSP avocado oil or olive oil
  • 1 tsp dijon mustard
  • 1 clove fresh garlic
  • ½ tsp fresh grated/minced ginger
  • ½ lime, juiced
  • ¼-½ tsp salt to taste

Instructions

PREP THE VEGGIES

  • Trim the ends from the snap peas and slice diagonally on a bias. You'll position your knife at 45 degrees from the snap peas to create a diamond-like shape that is oh so satisfying to eat by the forkful. Slice the green onions the same way.
  • Prep edamame as needed. You can buy your edamame already cooked and shelled *or* pick up a 10-12 oz package of whole edamame pods and cook them for a few minutes in boiling water. Then simply pop the seeds out of the shells and add them to your salad. I buy a costco-sized package of edamame pods every few months and shell my own. Either way will have delicious results!

MAKE THE DRESSING

  • Peel and mince a clove of garlic and squeeze the juice from half a lime.
  • Add dressing ingredients to a mason jar and shake well to combine. You can add extra rice vinegar or lime juice for a more tart dressing if desired.
  • You can dunk a snap pea into the dressing and taste test the acidity/sweetness then adjust to your liking.

SALAD TIME!

  • Add the veggies and half the shaken dressing to a large salad bowl and mix well. Taste and add any additional salt desired, then add as much of the remaining dressing as you'd like.
  • Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and enjoy!

Notes

Recipe yields 2 larger servings or 4 small side salads.
Nutrition Facts below are estimated for one of 2 servings (half the recipe) using an online recipe nutrition calculator. Adjust as needed and enjoy!

Nutrition

Calories: 383kcal, Carbohydrates: 32g, Protein: 17g, Fat: 22g, Saturated Fat: 3g, Polyunsaturated Fat: 5g, Monounsaturated Fat: 12g, Trans Fat: 0.01g, Sodium: 502mg, Potassium: 794mg, Fiber: 10g, Sugar: 16g, Vitamin A: 1333IU, Vitamin C: 82mg, Calcium: 177mg, Iron: 6mg

As written, this tasty salad is vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free, grain-free, dairy-free, and above all else, so flipping delicious!

Behind the Blog

I just finished watching the first season of The Institute which is pretty closely based on the Stephen King book of the same name. Season 2 drops in a month and I can’t wait! They’re extending it past where the book ends so I’m excited to see where it goes.

Book-wise I just read “Hell Bent” from Leigh Bardugo (★★★★★ amazing no notes) and after I mourn the ending of the trilogy (I didn’t want it to end!) I’m going to dive right into V.E. Schwab’s “Victorious” tomorrow which is (of course) another final book in a trilogy I’ve been loving for years. Clearly I have a type. I’m at the point where I’ve read absolutely everything both of these authors have written and will continue to pretty much forever.

What are you reading/watching lately? I need recommendations!

In other news, we finally (FINALLY!!!!) finished my pantry renovation and I’m super stoked to share it with y’all soon. I do a little happy dance whenever I open the door, and not just because there’s a giant jar of watermelon sour patch gummies sitting on the counter. Hah!
